verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's docs show flag targeting rules that serve variations based on context attributes, with segments as a targeting option and a documented path for converting rules into segments. Independent users corroborate the ordered, ANDed attribute rules and group-level targeting, and mention Big Segments. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of how segments are defined and reused across flags (the segment evidence is mostly page titles and brief mentions).

support.subject: As a developer, I can target flags with attribute-based rules and reusable segments so the right users see the right variation

citations.quote: This topic explains how to use flag targeting rules to serve flag variations to different contexts based on their attributes.
LaunchDarkly SDKs can pass any context attributes you want to LaunchDarkly, where you can then use those attributes in flag targeting.
In addition to targeting specific context attributes, you can target individuals, segments, or specific mobile apps and devices.
Create as many feature flags as you need and target them by user, segment, or rule.
LaunchDarkly's system (an ordered set of rules with ANDed conditions over arbitrary key/value contexts) arguably better than their internal mini expression language
